title: Autoglym Ultimate Screenwash vs Prestone Extreme Performance Screenwash

brand.product: Autoglym Ultimate Screenwash concentrate, 500 ml

key_ingredients.name: Screenwash concentrate, 1:9 for general use, claimed to -45 C neat

alternative.product: Prestone Extreme Performance Concentrated Screen Wash, 2.5 litres

key_ingredients.name: Screenwash concentrate, up to 1:19 in summer, usable neat in winter

summary: Both are strong screenwash concentrates, and Prestone won the Auto Express test the Autoglym came second in.
evidence: Auto Express, 1 September 2026, tested both mixed at 1:4. Prestone scored 5 of 5 and Autoglym 4.5 of 5. The pack sizes differ five times over, so compare them by the cost of a litre of mixed washer fluid: at 1:4 a litre uses 200 ml of concentrate. Auto Express's rounded prices at the time (we did not see them on a shelf) were around GBP 7 for 500 ml of Autoglym and around GBP 4.75 for 2.5 litres of Prestone, so 200 ml cost about GBP 2.80 with Autoglym and about 38p with Prestone.
differences: Autoglym's bottle is much smaller and easier to store. It stayed fluid and squirting after two hours in the freezer at 1:4, and it claims -45 C neat. Auto Express tested Prestone's freezing neat, where it stayed fluid, and reported its cleaning at 1:4, so we can't compare the two for frost at 1:4. Auto Express suggested the Autoglym best suits being a back-up. A Hagerty test from January 2023 gave the Autoglym 7 of 10 and it partly froze at -18 C.
why: Auto Express put Prestone first on freeze resistance and cleaning at a much lower cost per litre. Autoglym's main gain is a smaller bottle.

title: Autoglym Bodywork Shampoo vs Simoniz Shampoo & Wax

brand.product: Autoglym Bodywork Shampoo Conditioner, 1 litre

key_ingredients.name: pH neutral car shampoo, 2 capfuls per 10 litres, about 30p a wash in the test
Car shampoo with wax, about 13p a wash in the test

summary: Both are car shampoos from one Auto Express test, and the Simoniz scored higher, 4 of 5 against 3.5.
evidence: Auto Express, 8 January 2026, tested seven shampoos for foam, lubrication and oil-cutting, and worked out the cost per wash for a 10 litre bucket. Simoniz scored 4 of 5 and Autoglym 3.5 of 5. Autoglym's own site doses its shampoo at 2 capfuls per 10 litres. The magazine's rounded prices at the time were around GBP 10.49 for 1 litre of Autoglym (30p a wash) and around GBP 8.50 for 2 litres of Simoniz (13p a wash).
differences: Simoniz contains wax. Autoglym says its shampoo leaves existing wax or sealant intact, and the magazine did not test how either treats a protective coat. Auto Express said Autoglym's lubrication was just behind the leaders and Simoniz had a reasonable foam and a surprising level of lubrication. Neither won: Bilt-Hamber did. Tesco's cheaper shampoo scored lowest, with the worst lubrication, so we don't suggest it.
why: Auto Express scored the Simoniz higher overall at less than half the cost per wash. The score includes value, and the article doesn't rank the two against each other on lubrication alone.

aspects.aspect: Cost per wash in the test

title: Autoglym Polar Blast vs CarPlan Polar White Snow Foam

brand.product: Autoglym Polar Blast snow foam, 2.5 litres

key_ingredients.name: pH neutral snow foam, about 80p a wash in the test

alternative.product: CarPlan Polar White snow foam, 2.5 litres

key_ingredients.name: Snow foam, about 21p a wash in the test

summary: Both are 2.5 litre snow foams for a pressure washer, and the CarPlan scored higher in one Auto Express test.
evidence: Auto Express, 30 March 2026, sprayed each foam through the same lance onto a van unwashed for six months, left it 10 minutes and rinsed. CarPlan scored 4.5 of 5 and Autoglym 3 of 5. The magazine's rounded prices at the time were around GBP 23.99 for Autoglym (80p a wash), the same as on Autoglym's own site, and around GBP 10.55 for CarPlan (21p a wash).
differences: Autoglym states pH neutral and that it won't strip wax. The test article doesn't give CarPlan's pH, so if your car is waxed, check its label. Auto Express credited the Autoglym with strong cleaning and said the CarPlan cleans almost as well as the top two. Neither came first: Bilt-Hamber did.
why: Auto Express called the CarPlan the cheapest way to get a clean among the foams it tested, and it outscored the Autoglym.

title: Sonax ActiFoam Energy vs Triplewax Vortex Blast

brand.product: Sonax ActiFoam Energy snow foam, 1 litre

key_ingredients.name: Snow foam, 1:10 to 1:20 in a lance, about 76p a wash in the test

alternative.product: Triplewax Vortex Blast snow foam, 1 litre

key_ingredients.name: Snow foam, about 26p a wash in the test

summary: Both are 1 litre snow foams, and in one Auto Express test the Triplewax scored higher.
evidence: Auto Express, 30 March 2026, sprayed each foam through the same lance onto a van unwashed for six months, left it 10 minutes and rinsed. Triplewax scored 4.5 of 5 and Sonax 3.5 of 5. The magazine said Sonax's foam was decent at 1:10 but its cleaning trailed the best, and that Triplewax cleans just as well as CarPlan Polar White, which also scored 4.5. Its rounded prices at the time were around GBP 14.29 for Sonax (76p a wash) and around GBP 5.27 for Triplewax (26p a wash).
differences: Sonax says ActiFoam Energy also works as a shampoo, insect remover and wheel rim cleaner, and it sells a 5 litre pack. The test covered only snow foam use. We have no price on file for a bigger Triplewax pack.
why: Auto Express rated the Triplewax a full star above the Sonax for cleaning power and value, at about a third of the cost per wash.

title: Autoglym Intensive Tar Remover vs Angelwax Nemesis

brand.product: Autoglym Intensive Tar Remover, 500 ml

key_ingredients.name: Tar remover, apply with a cloth, leave 1 to 2 minutes
Tar remover

summary: Both are 500 ml tar removers, and Angelwax won the Auto Express test the Autoglym came second in.
evidence: Auto Express, 18 August 2026, tested ten on bitumen hardened on a scrap wing. Angelwax scored 5 of 5 and Autoglym 4.5 of 5. The magazine said the Angelwax was the fastest to melt the blobs and that the Autoglym was almost as quick but hard to justify at the higher cost. Its rounded prices at the time were around GBP 17.99 for Autoglym (the same on Autoglym's own site) and around GBP 10.95 for Angelwax.
differences: The Autoglym has a mild scent and is gentler on plastics, though its own FAQ says not to use it on interior plastics. The Angelwax smells strongly, so use it outdoors, and take care near plastic trim and matte paint. If your job is close to trim, the Autoglym has a real advantage.
why: On speed at dissolving tar the Angelwax beat the Autoglym in this test. What the extra money buys is a milder smell and gentler treatment of plastic.

title: Autoglym Active Insect Remover vs CarPlan No1 Super Bug

brand.product: Autoglym Active Insect Remover, 500 ml

key_ingredients.name: Foam insect remover, leave about 30 seconds
Gel insect remover

summary: Both are bug removers that Auto Express says are safe on wax, and CarPlan won the test with a bigger bottle.
evidence: Auto Express, 1 June 2026, tested fourteen on a scrap bonnet with real flies and a homemade stand-in baked on. CarPlan scored 5 of 5 and Autoglym 3.5 of 5, and the magazine described both as safe on wax. Its rounded prices at the time were around GBP 11 for 600 ml of CarPlan and around GBP 12 for Autoglym. Autoglym's own site listed GBP 11.99 for 500 ml, which we used here.
differences: Autoglym is a foam that clings without dribbling, and CarPlan is a gel that stayed put. Auto Express said the test paint was almost completely clear after one wipe of the CarPlan and called the Autoglym wax-safe but pricey. It didn't test either on glass or plastic, and Autoglym's site lists those surfaces as safe. We left out cheaper removers in this test that strip wax.
why: Auto Express rated the CarPlan a star and a half above the Autoglym, and both are described as safe on wax, so the Autoglym's higher price per ml brought no better result in this test.

aspects.aspect: Safe on wax, per Auto Express

title: Turtle Wax Clearvue vs Rain-X 2-in-1 Glass Cleaner + Repellent

brand.product: Turtle Wax Clearvue rain repellent, 300 ml

key_ingredients.name: Rain repellent, needs two coats

alternative.product: Rain-X 2-in-1 Glass Cleaner + Rain Repellent, 500 ml

key_ingredients.name: Glass cleaner and rain repellent, spray on and wipe off

summary: Auto Express gave both rain repellents the same score, and the Rain-X comes in a bigger bottle.
evidence: Auto Express, 8 April 2026, applied each to half a windscreen and a side window on four cars and drove them in the wet for four weeks. Both scored 4.5 of 5. It called the Rain-X superb value, and said the Turtle Wax was arguably slightly better but costs more for what you get. The magazine's rounded prices at the time were around GBP 7.50 for 300 ml of Turtle Wax and around GBP 4.98 for 500 ml of Rain-X.
differences: The Turtle Wax was one of only three still working well at the end of four weeks. The Rain-X was starting to wear away by then, so expect to apply it more often. The Turtle Wax needs two coats. The Rain-X also cleans the glass. Both lost to Gtechniq G5, which lasted better than either.
why: The magazine scored them level and the Rain-X is far cheaper per ml. The Turtle Wax's lead is lasting longer, so the swap suits anyone happy to reapply.

title: Ring Ultrainflate 20 vs RAC 12V Digital Air Compressor

brand.product: Ring Ultrainflate 20 digital tyre inflator (RTI120)

key_ingredients.name: 12V digital inflator, 3 m cable, 60 cm hose, stops at set pressure
12V digital inflator, over-read by half a PSI in the test

summary: Both are 12V digital tyre inflators from one Auto Express test, and the RAC came second to the Ring.
evidence: Auto Express, 8 October 2025, timed each on a 15 inch wheel from 10 to 35 PSI and checked the display against a calibrated gauge. Ring scored 5 of 5 and RAC 4.5 of 5. The RAC over-read by half a PSI and the Ring read 1 PSI out. The magazine said the RAC does all you need at a good price. Ring's own site confirms the 3 m cable and 60 cm hose. The magazine's rounded prices at the time were around GBP 39.99 for Ring and around GBP 16 for RAC.
differences: The Ring is faster, second quickest in the test, while the RAC took three minutes exactly. The Ring's cable and hose are among the longest in the test and are stored inside. The RAC's reach around a car was judged long enough, and its leads wrap around the back. When buying, check that the listing really is this RAC model, because the magazine's shop link had a different brand name in its address.
why: The RAC was closer to the true pressure than the Ring in this test and reaches round a car. What the Ring's extra cost buys is speed and tidier storage.

title: Ring Ultra Charge 10 vs Draper 12V Intelligent Charger

brand.product: Ring Ultra Charge 10 smart battery charger (RSC1010), 10 A

key_ingredients.name: 10 A output, 4.3 m cable, LCD, alternator test
10 A output, 3 m reach, IP65

summary: Both are 10 A smart car battery chargers, and the Draper won the Auto Express test.
evidence: Auto Express, 24 November 2025, charged a 68 Ah battery from 10.5 V, timed it to 80%, and tried a flat 95 Ah pack and a dead 5 Ah battery. Draper scored 5 of 5 and Ring 4.5 of 5. The magazine's rounded prices at the time were around GBP 99.98 for Ring and around GBP 71.98 for Draper. Its product awards of 15 April 2026 listed the Draper at around GBP 53, so its price may be lower now; we used the higher, older figure.
differences: The Ring was the fastest to 80%, by a few minutes. It has a longer 4.3 m cable, a colour LCD and an alternator tester, which the Draper is not described as having. Auto Express felt those extras don't justify the premium, and Ring quotes the same article saying it would pick the Ring if money were no object.
why: The output is the same 10 A and the Draper was narrowly behind on charging speed. What the Ring's extra cost mainly buys is its longer cable and alternator test.

title: Bosch AeroTwin vs Lucas Airflex Wiper Blades

brand.product: Bosch AeroTwin wiper blades, pair for a Fiat Panda (23 and 16 inch)

key_ingredients.name: Flat wiper blades

alternative.product: Lucas Airflex wiper blades, pair for a Fiat Panda (23 and 16 inch)

key_ingredients.name: Wiper blades

summary: Bosch won the Auto Express wiper test and the Lucas Airflex came close behind.
evidence: Auto Express, 4 September 2025, fitted seven pairs to a Fiat Panda after chilling them to -20 C and scored fitting, noise, judder and smearing on wet and dry screens. Bosch scored 5 of 5 and Lucas 4.5 of 5. The magazine said the Lucas came close to toppling the Bosch, with a smear-free wipe. Its rounded prices at the time were around GBP 25 for Bosch and around GBP 21 for Lucas, for this car's sizes; yours will differ.
differences: Bosch is better here. The AeroTwin was quiet and steady with no judder, and the Lucas was noisier, with a louder thump when changing direction. Fit depends on your car's arms, so check the Lucas fits before buying. The test didn't measure how long either lasts.
why: The Lucas wiped without smearing in the same test, so if a louder sweep doesn't bother you, the Bosch's premium buys quietness more than a clearer screen.

title: Angelwax Enigma AiO vs Sonax Xtreme Ceramic Polish All-in-One

brand.product: Angelwax Enigma AiO all-in-one polish, 500 ml

key_ingredients.name: All-in-one polish

alternative.product: Sonax Xtreme Ceramic Polish All-in-One, 500 ml

key_ingredients.name: All-in-one polish and seal, by hand or machine

summary: Both are 500 ml all-in-one polishes, and Sonax ranked above Angelwax on the final score.
evidence: Auto Express, 15 January 2026, worked each across a panel of a worn MG by hand and machine and scored shine, ease and value. Sonax scored 4.5 of 5 and Angelwax 4 of 5, and the verdict named Sonax second and Angelwax third. Sonax's own page says it polishes, smooths and seals in one step by hand or machine. The magazine's rounded prices at the time were around GBP 32.95 for Angelwax and around GBP 21.60 for Sonax.
differences: Angelwax is better on results. It topped the points table for this test and matched the winner's shine, and the magazine said it would be its pick if cost were no concern. Sonax's page gives two figures for protection, up to two months and up to three months, and the test did not measure how long protection lasts.
why: Sonax's polish does the same one-step job and the magazine called it a great job at a relatively low price for a ceramic formula. Pay for the Angelwax if the last bit of shine matters more than the price gap.

title: WD-40 Specialist Penetrant vs Rocket TT

brand.product: WD-40 Specialist Penetrant Smart Straw, 400 ml

key_ingredients.name: Penetrating spray with nozzle and straw
Penetrating spray

summary: Both are penetrating sprays for seized fixings, and Rocket TT won the Auto Express test.
evidence: Auto Express, 25 February 2026, soaked nuts and bolts in salt water and left them outdoors for over a year, sprayed each fluid on, and measured the torque to free them. Rocket TT scored 5 of 5 and freed the nut at the lowest torque; WD-40 Specialist Penetrant scored 4 of 5 with the third-lowest. The magazine's rounded prices at the time were around GBP 9.48 for 400 ml of WD-40 and around GBP 5.49 for 450 ml of Rocket TT. Toolstation listed the WD-40 at GBP 9.49 on 6 November 2026, the price we used here. The magazine's awards of 15 April 2026 listed Rocket TT at around GBP 6, which still leaves it about 44% cheaper per ml.
differences: The WD-40 was the easiest to use, with a praised nozzle and straw, and gave the third-lowest torque. Rocket TT climbed highest up the test nail, seeped quickly and freed the nut at the lowest torque, level with the much dearer Bulldog. We have no second test of Rocket TT, and the magazine's published results are rankings, without the torque figures.
why: Rocket TT beat the WD-40 on freeing a rusted nut in this test and costs about half as much per ml, so what the extra buys is an easier nozzle.

title: Knipex Assembly Combination Set vs Minotaur Hi-Leverage Pliers Set

brand.product: Knipex Assembly Combination Set, 3 pieces

key_ingredients.name: Three-piece plier set
160 mm combination, 160 mm diagonal, 200 mm long-nose, chrome vanadium steel, TPR grips

summary: Both are three-piece plier sets, and the Minotaur won the Auto Express test.
evidence: Auto Express, 13 October 2026, cut 6 mm wire and a large cable tie, gripped a hardened bolt and tried to hold a sheet of paper. Minotaur scored 5 of 5 and Knipex 3.5 of 5, though Knipex had the best cutters. The magazine's rounded prices at the time were around GBP 79.99 for Knipex and around GBP 14.99 for Minotaur, both per three-piece set. Toolstation listed the Minotaur at GBP 14.99 including VAT on 6 November 2026, with over 20 available.
differences: Knipex's cutters were the best in the test, gliding through the tie and wire with the least effort. Its standard pliers were stiff and failed to grip the paper. The Minotaur tools are smaller than some rivals and were described as gripping and cutting as hard as bigger ones. The article doesn't report a long-term wear test, so we can't say how either set lasts over years. If you cut wire all day, the Knipex cutters are worth a look.
why: For the jobs in this test the Minotaur set scored higher overall at less than a fifth of the price, though Knipex still had the best cutters.

title: Hammerite Kurust vs Nitromors Rust Converter

brand.product: Hammerite Kurust, 250 ml

key_ingredients.name: Rust converter, turns rust blue or black, topcoat after 3 hours
Rust converter, best painted over

summary: Both convert rust before painting, and the Nitromors won the Auto Express test the Kurust came sixth in.
evidence: Auto Express, 3 November 2026, treated rusted 1 mm steel, painted one face, then left the samples outside for four months with daily salt spray. Nitromors scored 4.5 of 5 and Kurust 2.5 of 5. The magazine's rounded prices at the time were around GBP 13 for 250 ml of Hammerite and around GBP 17.99 for 500 ml of Nitromors, so the bottle costs more and the cost per ml is lower.
differences: The Kurust worked fastest, turning rust black almost at once, and Hammerite sells a 90 ml size for small jobs. Hammerite says it's sold through selected stores and not online. The Nitromors had the lightest corrosion on the painted face, but its unpainted side showed clear rust, so paint over it. The Kurust's sample was rusty on the bare side and worn on the painted side. If you only have a stone chip, the small Kurust bottle may be all you need.
why: In four months of salt spray the Nitromors protected painted steel far better than the Kurust, and it costs less per ml.

title: Dremel 8150 vs Vonhaus Cordless Rotary Tool

brand.product: Dremel 8150 cordless rotary tool, 7.2 V

key_ingredients.name: 7.2 V, 2.0 Ah battery

alternative.product: Vonhaus Cordless Rotary Tool with Carry Case, 8 V

key_ingredients.name: 8 V, 2.5 Ah battery, 164 accessories, carry case

summary: Both are cordless rotary tools, and the Vonhaus won the Auto Express test the Dremel came third in.
evidence: Auto Express, 10 September 2026, drilled mild steel, cut a bolt, cleaned rust and buffed aluminium with each tool, and based value on the lowest online prices it found. Vonhaus scored 5 of 5 and Dremel 4 of 5. Dremel's UK blog confirms the 7.2 V brushless motor. The magazine's rounded prices at the time were around GBP 79.01 for Dremel and around GBP 29.99 for Vonhaus.
differences: The Dremel is stronger, with particularly impressive metal cutting, and the magazine said it feels built to last. The Vonhaus was described as not the most powerful, though it did well in every task. The Vonhaus comes with 164 accessories and the best carry case. The Dremel lacks a case and has few attachments for the price. Heavy metal work favours the Dremel.
why: For the mix of jobs tested the Vonhaus was the magazine's all-round pick at well under half the price, with more accessories. The Dremel's extra money buys power and a sturdier feel.

title: Ansell TouchNTuff vs Toolstation Blue Nitrile Gloves

brand.product: Ansell TouchNTuff disposable gloves, box of 100

key_ingredients.name: Disposable workshop gloves, thinner than most rivals in the test

alternative.product: Disposable Blue Powder-Free Nitrile Gloves, Large, box of 100

key_ingredients.name: Nitrile, powder-free, fully textured, EN ISO 374-5 and EN ISO 374-1 Type B

summary: Both are disposable workshop gloves in boxes of 100, and the Toolstation ones won the Auto Express test.
evidence: Auto Express, 8 October 2026, ordered each in large, tested them against petrol, WD-40, carburettor cleaner, engine oil and wheel cleaner, then dropped water-filled gloves onto a blunt nail. Toolstation's gloves scored 5 of 5 and Ansell's 4 of 5. Toolstation lists its gloves as nitrile, powder-free and certified to EN ISO 374-1 Type B. The magazine's rounded prices at the time were around GBP 24.99 per 100 for Ansell (25p each) and around GBP 13.28 per 100 for Toolstation (13p each). why: The Toolstation gloves did well on every test in the article at about half the Ansell's cost per glove, and the magazine noted the Ansell's price had gone up by a tenner in two years.

aspects.aspect: Cost per glove in the test

title: Big Wipes vs Hygimax Heavy Duty Cleaning Wipes

alternative.product: Hygimax Heavy Duty Cleaning Wipes, 100 wipes

key_ingredients.name: Heavy-duty cleaning wipes, about 9p each in the test

summary: Both are workshop hand-cleaning wipes, and Hygimax won the Auto Express test.
evidence: Auto Express, 4 June 2025, tried each on grease, diesel soot and bitumen underseal on a hard panel and on fabric, and on hands. Hygimax scored 5 of 5 and Big Wipes 3 of 5. The magazine said Hygimax alone made a real impact on the tar spots, and that Big Wipes struggled on fabric and made no dent on the tar. Its prices at the time, the oldest in this batch, were GBP 13.49 for 80 Big Wipes (17p each) and around GBP 8 for 100 Hygimax (9p each).

title: Evo-Stik Interior Resin Wood Glue vs SikaBond PVA Wood Adhesive+

brand.product: Evo-Stik Interior Resin Wood Glue, 1 litre

key_ingredients.name: Wood glue, EN 204 D1, interior only, dries clear
Wood glue, EN 204 D3, indoors and outdoors, dries clear

summary: Both are 1 litre resin wood glues at the same shop, and the Sika costs about 21% less and has the higher listed water rating.
evidence: Both read on toolstation.com on 6 November 2026, including VAT, with no reduction shown: Evo-Stik GBP 13.99 and Sika GBP 10.99 for 1 litre. Toolstation lists Evo-Stik's as complying with EN 204 D1 and Sika's as conforming to D3. Soudal's guide explains D1 as interior use only with wood moisture up to 15%, and D3 as interior use with frequent short exposure to water, with outdoor use allowed where the bond is sheltered. why: The Sika carries the higher D3 rating at a lower price on the same shelf, so the Evo-Stik's D1 rating gives no documented reason to pay more.

title: Dowsil DC785+ Sanitary Silicone vs Soudal Trade Sanitary Silicone

alternative.product: Soudal Trade Sanitary Silicone, white, 290 ml

Soudal GBP 5.30 on offer, down from GBP 5.95 for 290 ml, and we used the regular GBP 5.95 (2.1p per ml). title: Dulux Trade Diamond Matt vs Leyland Trade Hardwearing Matt, 5 litres

key_ingredients.name: Durable interior matt, up to 12 sq m per litre, listed as scrubbable

evidence: Both read on toolstation.com on 6 November 2026, including VAT, with no reduction shown: Dulux GBP 65.99 and Leyland GBP 36.79. Priced by stated coverage: up to 16 sq m per litre for Dulux (80 sq m, about 82p per sq m) and up to 12 for Leyland (60 sq m, about 61p per sq m). Dulux's own site confirms 16 and its scrub ratings. Toolstation lists the Leyland for kitchens, bathrooms and high-traffic areas.
differences: Dulux is much better documented: Class 1 under ISO 11998, Type C under BS 7719, tested to 10,000 scrubs, plus stain-repellent technology. Dulux also covers a third more per litre. No test we read compares them. If you need a proven scrub rating, stay with the Dulux.

title: Bosch Professional HSS-Co Set vs Metabo HSS-Co Set, 19 Pieces

title: Neudorff Ferramol Schneckenkorn vs Dehner Schneckenkorn

brand.product: Neudorff Ferramol Schneckenkorn, 2 kg

key_ingredients.name: Iron(III) phosphate
Iron(III) phosphate

summary: Both are slug pellets with iron(III) phosphate spread at 5 g per square metre, and the Dehner costs about 13% less per kilo at the same shop.
evidence: Both read on dehner.de on 6 November 2026, including VAT, shipping extra, both available online. Ferramol EUR 25.99 for 2 kg (EUR 13.00 per kg). Dehner EUR 13.49 for 1.2 kg (EUR 11.24 per kg). Neudorff's own page gives 9.9 g/kg of iron(III) phosphate and 5 g per sq m. Dehner's page gives the same active and the same rate without a strength. The approval numbers differ: 034496-00 for Ferramol and 008016-62 for Dehner.
differences: Because Dehner's page doesn't state the strength, we can't call these the same active at the same strength. Neudorff sells smaller packs, down to 200 g, and we didn't see their prices. The UK's Royal Horticultural Society advises against slug pellets, including organic ones, because of harm to garden wildlife, so try other ways first. No test we read covers these two.
why: Same active ingredient and same application rate on both pages, and the Dehner costs less per kilo in the pack sizes we could price. The saving is modest, so it mainly matters if you use a lot.

title: Gorilla Duct Tape vs Uline Heavy Duty Duct Tape

brand.product: Gorilla Duct Tape, 2 in x 30 yds, silver

key_ingredients.name: 16 mil, natural rubber adhesive, 50 lb tensile, actual width 1.88 in

alternative.product: Uline Heavy Duty Duct Tape, 2 in x 60 yds, silver

key_ingredients.name: 14.5 mil, high-tack natural rubber adhesive, 30 lb tensile

summary: Both are thick silver duct tapes at Uline, and Uline's heavy-duty roll costs about 39% less per yard, with a lower tensile rating than Gorilla.
evidence: Both read on uline.com on 6 November 2026, both in stock. Gorilla $16 for 30 yards at one roll (53 cents a yard). Uline $19.45 for 60 yards at the 4 roll minimum (32 cents a yard). A half case of 12 Uline rolls is $18.70 a roll, $224.40 in all, a count we worked out from the 24 per case. Thickness is 16 mil against 14.5 mil, and both use natural rubber adhesive.
differences: Gorilla is stronger on paper: 50 lb tensile against 30 lb, and slightly thicker. It has a two-year shelf life against one year, and you can buy a single roll, while Uline needs four, which is $77.80 before shipping. Gorilla's maker also claims double-thick adhesive and UV resistance. For jobs needing the most strength, stay with the Gorilla.
why: If you get through a lot of heavy tape, the Uline gives twice the length per roll at a lower cost per yard and is nearly as thick. The Gorilla's extra money buys higher tensile strength and a longer shelf life.

21.5 cm bypass, SK5 carbon steel, 25 mm cut, sap groove, wire notch, replaceable blades and spring

title: Vitax Q4 vs Growmore General Fertiliser

brand.product: Vitax Q4 fertiliser, 2.5 kg

key_ingredients.name: Granular general feed, NPK 5.3-7.5-10 with trace elements
Granular general feed, NPK 7-7-7, up to 46 sq m per pack

summary: The RHS names both as general-purpose garden fertilisers, and at Crocus the Growmore costs about 48% less per kilo, with less potash than the Q4.
evidence: Both read on crocus.co.uk on 6 November 2026, with no reduction shown, both in stock: Vitax Q4 GBP 11.99 for 2.5 kg (GBP 4.80 a kg) and Growmore GBP 9.99 for 4 kg (GBP 2.50 a kg). The RHS growing guide for asters says to use a general-purpose fertiliser such as Growmore or Vitax Q4. Crocus lists NPK 5.3-7.5-10 with trace elements for Q4 and 7-7-7 for Growmore.
differences: The analysis isn't the same. Q4 has more potash and trace elements, and Crocus suggests it for roses and for tomatoes and chrysanthemums every 3 to 4 weeks. Growmore has more nitrogen. For fruit and flowers that want potash, stay with Q4 or use a potash feed. Crocus names no maker for this Growmore. Crocus gives no weight-per-area rate for either. The RHS guide says a handful per square metre.
why: For a general spring feed the RHS aster guide names either one, and the Growmore is about half the price per kilo. Crocus suggests Q4 for tomatoes and roses, so keep it for those.

title: Gorilla Super Glue vs Everbuild GP Super Glue

Medium-viscosity super glue, sets in about 5 to 15 seconds, for plastics, metals, PVCu, EPDM and glass

summary: Both are super glues at the same shop, and the Everbuild costs about 72% less per gram in a bigger pack.
evidence: Both read on toolstation.com on 6 November 2026, including VAT, with no reduction shown on either page: Gorilla GBP 7.99 for 15 g (53p a gram) and Everbuild GBP 2.99 for 20 g (15p a gram). The 50 g Everbuild was GBP 4.59 (9p a gram). Neither page names the chemistry. The name super glue generally means cyanoacrylate.

If the repair will take knocks, Gorilla's documented claim may be worth having.
why: For a small repair on hard plastic, metal or glass the Everbuild is listed for those materials and sets faster by its page, at under a third of the price per gram. Gorilla's main documented extra is impact resistance.
